title: Point-to-Point Source–Channel Separation

items.title: Finite-alphabet point-to-point joint source-channel codes
items.statement: Defines a deterministic block encoder from a finite IID source block to a finite DMC input block and a deterministic decoder from the channel output block to a finite reproduction block; fixes the source-symbol/channel-use ratio and distinguishes lossless, expected-distortion, and positive-slack excess-distortion criteria.
items.strategy: Specify finite alphabets, source law, DMC transition law, deterministic maps, induced block law, blocklength ratio, and distinct performance criteria.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy, MIT OpenCourseWare 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 20: Advanced Channel Coding and Source-Channel Separation
Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, author-hosted full text

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all source, channel, and reproduction alphabets are finite.

items.title: Finite-IID lossless source coding above entropy
items.statement: For a finite IID source with entropy H in nats and every rate R>H, constructs deterministic fixed-length source codes with block error tending to zero and limiting superior log-message rate below R.
items.strategy: Use the finite-alphabet self-information typical set, Chebyshev's inequality proved by a pointwise square bound, a typical-set cardinality estimate, and a deterministic injective labeling.
proof_obligations: Show the empirical self-information exceeds H+delta with probability tending to zero, directly from the finite variance and the pointwise square bound.
Bound the typical-set cardinality by exp(k(H+delta)).
Construct a deterministic fixed-length encoder/decoder with error at most the atypical probability and rate below R.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the typical sets and all codebooks are finite.

items.title: Finite-IID rate-distortion mutual-information converse
items.statement: For an IID finite-alphabet source and any finite block reconstruction with expected distortion D_k, proves ln(2) times the single-letter information rate-distortion value in bits is at most k^{-1} I(S^k;S-hat^k) in nats, by finite time-sharing and chain-rule single-letterization.
items.strategy: Use the conditional reproduction test channel, the IID chain rule, coordinate projections, a uniform time-sharing index, and explicit bit-to-nat conversion.
proof_obligations: Construct the single-letter conditional reproduction channel induced by a uniformly chosen coordinate, including arbitrary rows on zero-probability source letters.
Show each coordinate mutual information is bounded by the corresponding chain-rule term using IID independence and nonnegative conditional mutual information.
Show mutual information of the time-shared pair is no larger than the average coordinate mutual information.
Apply the feasible-test-channel definition and convert bits to nats.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all alphabets, conditional laws, and time-sharing variables are finite.

items.title: Lossless separation for finite IID sources and finite DMCs
items.statement: For a finite IID source of entropy H nats, a finite DMC of capacity C nats/use, and channel-use ratio rho, reliable lossless transmission is achievable if H<rho C (and trivially if H=0); every reliable sequence must satisfy H<=rho C. No positive-entropy equality case is asserted.
items.strategy: Compose a typical-set source compressor with maximal-error DMC codes for achievability; use finite Markov data processing, the n-letter DMC information bound, and Fano's inequality for the converse.
proof_obligations: Handle the zero-entropy source with a constant decoder, including a zero-capacity channel.

Choose a source-code rate and maximal-error channel-code rate with strict margin below rho C, align them along the prescribed blocklength sequence, and bound the composite error without assuming a uniform source-code index.
Apply Fano's inequality to the source block and bound the information across the DMC by nC.
State explicitly that the positive-entropy equality boundary is not decided.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all alphabets and codebooks are finite.

items.title: Lossy separation for finite IID sources and finite DMCs
items.statement: For a finite IID source, finite reproduction alphabet, bounded finite distortion, feasible D, finite DMC capacity C nats/use, and channel-use ratio rho, let r(D)=ln(2)R(D) be the finite information rate-distortion function converted from bits to nats. Expected distortion and positive-slack excess-distortion criteria are separately achievable if r(D)<rho C, and either criterion implies r(D)<=rho C. If R(D)=0 a constant-reproduction code achieves both criteria; the positive-rate equality boundary is not asserted.
items.strategy: Use the finite-alphabet rate-distortion coding theorem and maximal-error channel codes for achievability; use the local single-letter mutual-information converse, the n-letter DMC information bound, bounded distortion, monotonicity, and right-continuity for the converse.
proof_obligations: Treat the zero-rate RDF case by constructing an independent zero-information test channel and a constant reproduction whose expected distortion is at most D.
For positive RDF strictly below rho C, choose a source-code rate and a maximal-error channel-code rate with strict margin, then align the blocklengths.
Bound composed expected distortion by the source-code distortion plus d_max times maximal channel error; bound excess probability by a source excess event plus channel error.
Single-letterize arbitrary block mutual information using the local IID time-sharing lemma and compare it with nC.
Use bounded distortion to pass from positive-slack excess probability to an expected-distortion bound, then use right-continuity at D.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all alphabets, conditional laws, and codebooks are finite.

summary: Define deterministic finite-alphabet joint source-channel block codes and prove lossless and lossy asymptotic separation for finite IID sources, finite DMCs, and feasible rate-distortion budgets. Use maximal-error channel codes because the compressed source index is generally nonuniform. Bounded distortion controls channel-error cost; positive-slack excess distortion remains distinct from expected distortion. No finite-block, zero-delay, or universal matching claim is made.

title: Point-to-Point Source–Channel Separation — Examples

items.title: A finite-alphabet source-channel rate budget
items.statement: For an IID Bernoulli(1/4) source and a BSC(1/4), computes the exact source entropy and channel capacity and verifies that five channel uses per source symbol give a strict asymptotic lossless margin.
proof_obligations: Compute I(X;Y) for an arbitrary Bernoulli input to the BSC and maximize it using finite KL nonnegativity.
Evaluate the source entropy and capacity exactly at crossover/source parameter 1/4.
Verify the strict rate inequality at ratio five by an exact integer comparison.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all entropy and capacity calculations are finite.

items.title: Strict asymptotic separation need not give zero finite-block error
items.statement: Refutes the claim that a strict entropy-capacity inequality guarantees a zero-error code at each finite blocklength ratio: a uniform binary source over a full-support BSC has positive error under every finite deterministic code, even when the asymptotic threshold is strict.
proof_obligations: Compute the exact positive entropy-capacity gap for the Bernoulli(1/2), BSC(1/4), six-use model.
For every finite deterministic code, exhibit a positive-probability source/output event on which the decoder is wrong, using full support of the BSC.
Separate the asymptotic reliability conclusion from finite-block zero error.
